author: simulation_agent

inequalities.inequality: sqrt(2*D*dt) << sigma at the stiffest point
dt << gamma/k_t at the stiffest point

numbers.name: trap_relaxation_time_min
numbers.note: gamma/k_t at the stiff end, the shortest time the integrator must resolve

numbers.name: dt_resolution_factor
numbers.note: how far below the shortest resolved time the step sits: two decades, the usual margin for an overdamped integrator, a convention and not a derivation

numbers.name: dt_max_relaxation
numbers.note: dt << gamma/k_t at the stiff end, the shortest time in the problem. Per point it is a hundredth of the LOCAL relaxation time, which is why it varies with the stiffness

numbers.name: noise_step_fraction
numbers.note: the rms noise displacement per step as a fraction of the thermal width

numbers.name: dt_max_noise
numbers.note: sqrt(2*D*dt) << sigma. NOT AN INDEPENDENT BOUND: sigma**2 = D*tau_t exactly, so this is dt << tau_t again with a different factor. Kept so a reader who expects two bounds finds why there is one

assumptions.statement: Two decades below the shortest resolved time is the usual margin for an overdamped integrator. A convention; no timestep scan has been run on this configuration.
assumptions.falsifier: a timestep scan showing the width flat over a wider range of steps replaces the factor with a measured one

assumptions.statement: A tenth of the thermal width per step. Dependent on the relaxation bound only because the declared potential is exactly harmonic; a trap that flattens away from its centre would separate them again.
assumptions.falsifier: a non-quadratic trap makes this a distinct bound

note: S4 takes the tighter, which is the noise bound by its factor. With no flow the drift bound that decided the driven configuration is absent, so the step here is a decade looser than there at the same stiffness.
